newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada lumber exports may hit quarterly limit.
newsitem.headline: Canada lumber exports may hit quarterly limit.

text.p: Canadian softwood lumber exports to the United States may reach the quarterly limit by September 27, after which lumber shipments will be slapped with an export fee, Canada's Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade said on Monday.

"Please advise your membership that on the basis of the current level of shipments we might be into a fee situation by September 27," Claudio Valle, director of the Special Trade Policy Division at the department, said in a news release.
"Shippers who may be concerned about attracting a fee charge are urged to continue to exercise caution," he said.

Under an agreement between Ottawa and Washington, export fees will be imposed on Canadian lumber exports exceeding 14.7 billion board feet per year or 4.226 billion board feet per quarter. The agreement became effective on April 1.
So far, in the second quarter (July-September) Canada has exported 3.71 billion of board feet of lumber, or 25.2 percent of the annual quota.
Quarterly exports are limited to 28.75 percent of the annual quota, after which export fees become effective. --Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
